original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-category-summands-finite-free}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Set $R = \Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. The category of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules which are summands of finite free
$\mathcal{O}$-modules is equivalent to the category of
finite projective $R$-modules.

final_content.statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), the monoidal category (D(O),⊗^L_O,O) contains an **invertible** object M when some N satisfies M⊗^L_O N≅O (and equivalently N⊗^L_O M≅O). An invertible O_n-module is an O_n-module locally free of rank 1. A family (O_n) of ring sheaves giving O≅∏_nO_n is *locally finite* when after a covering of each site object only finitely many component rings remain nonzero; shifts H^n[-n] are in the cohomological convention. A direct summand of a finite free O-module need not be globally free. Put R=Γ(C,O) the global section ring, and let global sections act on O-summands.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Set $R = \Gamma(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$. The category of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules which are summands of finite free
$\mathcal{O}$-modules is equivalent to the category of
finite projective $R$-modules.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site and R=Γ(C,O).
conclusions: The category of O-modules which are direct summands of finite free O-modules is equivalent to the category of finite projective R-modules.

semantic_review_note: For R=Γ(C,O), modules which are direct summands of finite free O-modules are categorically equivalent to finite projective R-modules, via global sections and extension of scalars. No assertion that all locally free finite sheaves are globally summands is introduced.
